events.title: King John of England Dies
events.description: King John died at Newark. He left the throne to his nine-year-old son, who became Henry III. John had sealed Magna Carta the year before, and his kingdom was in the middle of a civil war.
events.significance: His death eased the baronial rebellion. Under Henry III, Magna Carta was reissued and gradually became a cornerstone of English constitutional law.

events.title: Cornwallis Surrenders at Yorktown
events.description: British Major General Lord Cornwallis surrendered his army at Yorktown, Virginia, to George Washington and the French commander Comte de Rochambeau. The surrender followed a siege by combined American and French forces.
events.significance: It was the last major land battle of the American Revolutionary War. It paved the way for peace negotiations and British recognition of American independence.

events.title: John Jay Becomes First Chief Justice
events.description: John Jay was sworn in as the first Chief Justice of the United States. He led a Supreme Court that was still new and had few precedents.
events.significance: Jay helped set up the federal judiciary as a co-equal branch of government. That role shaped how the U.S. court system developed.

events.title: First Ascent of Cho Oyu
events.description: Pasang Dawa Lama of Nepal and the Austrians Herbert Tichy and Joseph Jöchler reached the summit of Cho Oyu. It is one of the world's highest peaks and lies on the Nepal–Tibet border.
events.significance: The climb was an early success in the golden age of Himalayan mountaineering. Cho Oyu is the sixth-highest mountain on Earth.

events.title: Saddam Hussein's Trial Begins
events.description: The Iraqi Special Tribunal opened the trial of Saddam Hussein and seven co-defendants on charges of crimes against humanity. Hussein had been Iraq's president for decades before he was deposed.
events.significance: The trial was a landmark moment for Iraq after the 2003 invasion. It ended with Hussein's conviction and his execution on December 30, 2006.
